comparisons.explanation: Specialist services, supervision, insurance and fixed staffing costs may matter even at small sites. Whether each current requirement is necessary or proportionate needs its actual written basis and priced scope.

The operator may have been used as the accountable grantee for reporting and reimbursement. This is a possible explanation; the record does not establish why the recipient changed or whether TVS could meet the conditions.
Community management with separately purchased specialist support, a shared administrator, or an amended grantee arrangement are alternatives to test, not authorized or funded replacements.

Hope was historically appointed, and opening publicity may repeat that identity. Such statements cannot settle the user-reported later operator change or current cost barrier.
A smaller mixed-period historical budget neither disproves a higher current proposal nor verifies it. Terms and scope must match before comparing.
Developer/press opening statements are retained as contrary context; variable or stale page wording and repeated Hope identification do not authenticate a current operator or occupancy.

output.summary: No current replacement-operator priced proposal, signed replacement agreement, actual staff roster or dated occupancy record was obtained. The roughly $1 million annual demand and resulting blockage remain a user-reported lead; neither verified nor disproved by the older budget. The precise City staff decision and legal basis requiring an operational service provider are not identified in the inspected report; community stewardship eligibility was not resolved. Actual City disbursements to Hope, pass-through to TVS, unpaid builder costs, unspent balances and a transfer/re-award decision remain unverified. Formal safeguards, proposed service staffing and an insurance statement do not establish actual resident protection or successful admission.
